status: literature findings; no implementation or performance validation

findings.claim: Acumen OSDI 2026 constructs strong snapshot consistency using signed per-user state descriptors, reconstruction and verification of missing operations, plus secure causal-stability garbage collection. This is a concrete document protocol, not a generic proof of arbitrary CBCL folds. Source: https://www.usenix.org/system/files/osdi26-cottone.pdf sections 5.2 and 5.3

Acumen Appendix D reports Snapdoc subset-omission weakness: valid snapshots can omit content without corresponding deletion operations. Earlier summaries of Snapdoc should not imply exact snapshot completeness. This is the Acumen authors analysis, not independently reproduced here. Source: https://www.usenix.org/system/files/osdi26-cottone.pdf Appendix D

IntegriDB verifies query completeness and aggregates over authenticated owner datasets, including JOIN SUM MAX/MIN COUNT and AVG. Candidate kernel adaptation must additionally authenticate the accepted causal cut and distributed updates. Source: https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/cpap/published/IntegriDB.pdf

Fraud-proof protocols can bisect disputed execution to one step; fast provisional loading requires available data, honest challengers and defined dispute resolution, and does not itself provide immediate offline correctness. Source: https://specs.optimism.io/fault-proof/

PeerReview uses signed logs and deterministic replay to detect and attribute misbehavior; it offers eventual accountability, not immediate proof that a loaded snapshot is correct. Source: https://www.mpi-sws.org/tr/2007-003.pdf

Nova provides incrementally verifiable computation via folding; can move work away from cold-open, but proving overhead and CBCL admission/causality encoding still need measurement. Source: https://eprint.iacr.org/2021/370
